generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: BRINGING LOCAL MODELS AND SANDBOXED TOOLS TO WINDOWS AND GITHUB COPILOT
Summary: GitHub Copilot is introducing support for local inference models and sandboxed tool execution on Windows devices, coordinated automatically with cloud models through intelligent orchestration. To enable this, Microsoft AI developed a quantized local version of the coding-optimized MAI Code 1.1 Flash model running on NVIDIA RTX Spark hardware with unified memory. Additionally, Microsoft Execution Containers provide operating-system-level sandboxing to secure shell commands and local server interactions during agentic workflows.

Editorial idea:
The next phase of coding assistants divides work between local capability and cloud capability while sandboxing keeps autonomous actions contained.

Central subject:
A developer workflow in which a local model handles nearby code while a separate contained workspace handles tool execution.

Visual relationship:
The story's tension is between responsiveness and reach: local inference keeps work close to the device, while cloud coordination and sandboxed tools expand what the agent can do without giving it unrestricted access.

Composition:
Show one continuous development workspace crossing from a Windows desktop area into a clearly bounded execution area, with code review and tool activity passing between them through a controlled gateway. Keep the human developer present as the person supervising the boundary, not as a decorative operator.

Permitted literal elements:
Windows development workspace
local model inference on the device
cloud model coordination
sandboxed shell or local-server execution area
developer reviewing the workflow boundary

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
server racks
generic chips
robots
cloud icons
shields
arrows
charts
logos
rendered text
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting local and cloud models as interchangeable without showing their different roles
Making the sandbox look like a generic cybersecurity lock rather than an execution boundary
Showing autonomous action without human oversight
Adding hardware specifications or interface details not stated in the source

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
